NZD/USD sentiment questions

Are retail traders long or short NZD/USD?

The live split for this pair is in the QDB Sheet. The page updates every weekday at about 5pm UK.

Why read retail sentiment as contrarian?

Most retail traders lose, and they tend to buy falling markets and sell rising ones. When the crowd piles onto one side, the stops and losing positions on that side become fuel for a move the other way. That is why a crowd that is heavily long is read as bearish.

Should I trade on sentiment alone?

No. A crowd can stay wrong for a long time. QDB only acts on sentiment at strong daily or weekly supply and demand levels, and treats it as one input next to the QDB Score and the COT positioning above.

What is the QDB Score?

A 0 to 12 score for each pair that combines retail positioning, how it is shifting and the trend. 7 or more reads bullish, 3 or less bearish. The guides explain how it works.
